_comment: Content calendar for Southbound 35. Each entry is one Monday-morning slot at 5 AM CT. status: 'live' | 'review' | 'drafted' | 'planned' | 'open'. Review-rule: no entry moves to 'live' without W. Scott Langford's explicit review of the PDF.
review_rule: No post goes live without Scott's review of the PDF
scope: Four pillars only: public-finance, economic-development, econometric-analysis, program-evaluation. Detour track (sports/religion/off-topic politics) retired June 2026.
build_order: Concentric from San Marcos for pillar-2 corridor work: Ring 0 (deeper Hays) -> Ring 1 (Comal first, then Caldwell/Guadalupe/S-Travis/E-Blanco) -> Ring 2 (Williamson, Bexar Northside, Bastrop). Pillar-1 mechanics, pillar-3 stats, and pillar-4 evaluations interleaved.

calendar.title: How a Texas Property Tax Bill is Built
calendar.notes: PDF in ~/Dropbox/southbound-35-drafts/01_*.pdf

calendar.title: Eanes ISD and Robin Hood: How Recapture Actually Works
calendar.notes: PDF in ~/Dropbox/southbound-35-drafts/02_*.pdf. Eanes is in Travis (Ring 1 by some measures) but the post is a pillar mechanics piece, not a corridor case study.

calendar.title: Eighty Miles: A Short History of the I-35 Corridor
calendar.notes: PDF in ~/Dropbox/southbound-35-drafts/03_*.pdf. Covers the corridor Hays sits in the middle of — frames the next several posts.

calendar.title: Sales tax 101: the second-biggest local revenue line
calendar.notes: Replaces a former detour slot. Pillar-1 sales-tax mechanics post: state 6.25, local-option 2.0 cap (1.0 city + various), Type A/B EDC slices, MTA/ATD slices, the SPD designation. Sets up later program-evaluation work on Type A/B EDCs.

calendar.title: San Marcos and Texas State: an enrollment-finance feedback loop
calendar.notes: Post A1 in next-series-outline.md. Ring 0. The most distinctive Hays story the macro series didn't tell. Touches author's employer — A2 question in outline asks about heads-up procedure before this one ships.

calendar.title: Kyle and Buda: the corridor's fastest-growing pair
calendar.notes: Post A2 in outline. Ring 0. Pairs nicely with the I-35 corridor history post just before.

calendar.title: Type A and Type B EDCs: what the audits show
calendar.notes: Replaces a former detour slot. Pillar-4 evaluation. Local-option sales-tax-funded economic development corporations (Chapters 504/505 Local Gov Code). Read the published audits and required project reports; ask what they say about effectiveness on their own terms.

calendar.title: Three districts, three school-finance worlds
calendar.notes: Post A3 in outline. Hays CISD / San Marcos CISD / Dripping Springs ISD. Ring 0. Makes the abstract recapture mechanics concrete with three districts within fifteen miles.

calendar.title: The western Hays Hill-Country edge
calendar.notes: Post A4 in outline. Ring 0. Companion to Kyle/Buda — same county, opposite end.

calendar.title: Truth-in-Taxation 101: reading the worksheets
calendar.notes: Property-tax mechanics series post 3 of 3. Timing matches statewide TIT hearings (Aug-Sep). Walks through a real TIT worksheet line by line — uses a San Marcos / Hays CISD worksheet.

calendar.title: The Comal growth story
calendar.notes: Comal series post 1 of 5. Ring 1. First step out from Hays.

calendar.title: Bond-election turnout: what the Texas data show
calendar.notes: Pillar-3 statistical analysis. Texas SOS turnout files. Bond elections have notoriously low + idiosyncratic turnout. Originally framed as a 'politics' detour; now framed as an applied analysis of turnout in low-information elections.

calendar.title: Comal projections, with the aquifer caveat
calendar.notes: Comal series post 2 of 5.

calendar.title: Comal water and the Edwards Aquifer Authority
calendar.notes: Comal series post 3 of 5. The single richest piece of the series. EAA permit system, J17 well, drought rules, HCP.

calendar.title: MUDs explained: the special-district mechanics
calendar.notes: First post in the special-districts pillar series. Why they exist, how they're created, how they finance, the lifecycle. Uses corridor MUDs (Hays + Comal) as examples — concrete from the start.

calendar.title: Comal schools and Comal ISD's bond posture
calendar.notes: Comal series post 4 of 5.

calendar.title: HB 3 compression: what changed for school M&O
calendar.notes: Replaces a former detour slot. Pillar-4 evaluation. HB 3 (86R, 2019) compressed school M&O rates via increased state funding. What did the rate path actually look like? What did per-pupil revenue do? Identification limits noted explicitly.

calendar.title: Who governs Comal County?
calendar.notes: Comal series post 5 of 5. Closes the Ring-1 first county.

calendar.title: Bond election preview: corridor edition
calendar.notes: Annual cycle: preview the major bond elections in the corridor counties before the Nov uniform election date. Cover school, county, and city bonds; show historical pass rates.

calendar.title: Caldwell County: the slow-growth neighbor
calendar.notes: Begin the next Ring-1 series. Caldwell is directly east of Hays — closer than Comal — but smaller and slower-growing. Open question (in outline) whether Caldwell goes before or after Comal.
